## Verdict: REJECT (one Important finding: a published example of an error message that the code never prints)

This branch is not ready to merge yet, because the new public rule-sets page tells readers to look for an error path in a form the loader never produces, and one wrong instruction in a troubleshooting page sends every reader who hits that error down a dead end.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. In `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 69, the page tells the reader that a rule-set file error "names the exact place in the file, for example `rule_sets.0.tables.1.columns`", but `_record_path` in `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 268 to 275 writes list positions in square brackets, so the message the reader actually sees is `rule_sets[0].tables[1].columns`. A reader who searches their output for the documented form finds nothing. The project's own tests in `tests/unit/test_cli_rule_sets.py` and `tests/unit/test_rule_set_file.py` assert the bracket form. (raised by 3/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: the subject is the sentence itself, an example of an error path, and making it true would change no output, no branch taken and no covered set — no mechanism's coverage is in dispute; no tool, lint, build step or agent-instruction file reads docs/external/rule-sets.md for behavior; the page is published customer-facing documentation, so limb two does not hold and the cap lands at Important -->

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (21)

<details><summary>21 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/cli.py` line 167 separates `_unconfirmed_rule_sets` from the function above it with one blank line, where every other top-level definition in the file uses two. Ruff's default rule selection does not flag this, so CI stays green. (raised by 2/6 agents)
2. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 99 says that `sqllens serve` and `sqllens validate` both "print a warning" for an unconfirmed set. Only `validate` prints to the console; `serve` emits the warning through the `sqllens.rule_sets` logger, so whether the operator sees it depends on the configured log level. (raised by 2/6 agents)
3. In `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 433 to 441, `_logged_by_guard` treats any cause that is not `UnsafeSqlError` or `RlsError` as already logged, so a refusal raised by the RLS parse branch in `src/sqllens/safety/rls.py` line 215 is both redacted to the generic kind and never written to the log. Every other guard logs its own fail-closed path first. The path is hard to reach, because the rule-set guard reparses and regenerates the statement before RLS sees it. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. In `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py` lines 76 to 84, `_RuleSetUserResolver` falls back to the shared built-in user, with no log record, whenever no rule-set selection is published. Every other rule-set component treats a missing selection as an error. Today's shipped call paths always publish one, so the behavior is correct; the asymmetry is what the reviewer flagged. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. In `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 752 to 774, `RuleSetsConfig` can hold a `file` value with no loaded rule sets, and every downstream gate keys off the loaded value rather than the file value. A `RuleSetsConfig` built outside `Config` validation would therefore disable the guard while the operator's configuration still names a rule-set file. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. In `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 234 to 248, `CatalogConfirmation` builds an `asyncio.Lock` at configuration-load time, outside any running event loop, and `ensure_catalog_confirmed` enters that lock outside the `try` block that turns failures into a structured refusal. A second event loop in the same process would surface the resulting error as an unstructured crash. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. In `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 467 to 472, `RefusalRedactingRunner` rebuilds the refusal with `type(exc).__new__` and a bare `Exception.__init__`, which skips the exception type's own constructor. It is safe today because the only subclass carrying state is re-raised earlier, but a future subclass with state would be returned half-built. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` lines 185 and 191 still state the runner call order without the two new runners, and `docs/internal/agent/factory.md` line 87 and `docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md` line 209 do the same. The change scoped one sibling line in the same file but left these unconditional ones, so they now read as complete orders that a rule-set configuration contradicts. (raised by 1/6 agents)
9. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 125 says every identifier is a decimal string, so `"5"` and `5` are written the same way. That holds for a request value, which the code folds to text, but not for the file itself, where a bare number fails validation. The sentence sits in advice that points the reader at the file's `binding.account_ids`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
10. The module docstring at `tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py` line 8 describes the example set as listing a predicate column, but the module's shared example mapping carries no predicate columns; individual tests supply one. (raised by 1/6 agents)
11. `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` line 3 records a freshness marker two commits behind the branch head, which is itself this branch's documentation commit. (raised by 1/6 agents)
12. `docs/external/configuration.md` line 234 still says that, unlike other sections, an unrecognized key inside a row-rule block is rejected at load. The new rule-sets section added by this change rejects unknown keys too, which adds another counterexample to that framing. (raised by 1/6 agents)
13. The architecture tree in `AGENTS.md` gains no entry for the two new modules, `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` and `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py`, although it lists the safety package file by file and is the file coding agents read first. (raised by 1/6 agents)
14. `src/sqllens/preflight.py` lines 168 to 174 turn any non-mismatch failure of the catalog check into a structured preflight error, and no test covers that branch. The documented case it protects is a database user that cannot read the catalog tables. (raised by 1/6 agents)
15. `src/sqllens/cli.py` lines 105 to 118 decide whether `verify-memory` adds its "does not support rule sets yet" message when the configuration failed to load, and neither the environment-variable branch nor the unreadable-file branch has a test. (raised by 1/6 agents)
16. Nothing drives the agent's SQL tool end to end to check that a rule-set refusal reaches the model with the prefix the new prompt rule keys on, named in `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` line 59. The existing test only compares the prompt text with the constant. (raised by 1/6 agents)
17. The two "nothing else changes" criteria have no regression test: nothing asserts that `list_data_sources` still answers a call carrying no request metadata while a rule-set file is configured, and nothing asserts that the bundle manifest gains no rule-set entry. (raised by 1/6 agents)
